answer.rationale: Finance mandate forces an 18% price cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price. Incumbent memory (c1, c6) is therefore non-actionable for cost this cycle. memory_c3 shows that the constrained component was previously stabilized by adding a second source during a shortage; that experience directly maps to today's 'no buffer, single primary, 14-day expiry' risk profile. I want to verify c3 first because it is the load-bearing precedent for splitting volume and protecting the line during a transition. I am not committing to a full switch yet; the action is a small, guarded primary-vendor move: shift a portion of primary volume to the low-cost vendor (c2) on a short pilot, keep the incumbent on a month-to-month tail (c5) until the pilot proves out, and retain optionality to add a true second source if the pilot meets cost and on-time targets. This minimizes TCO while delivery risk stays bounded by the month-to-month incumbent tail and the 94% volume cushion.
